mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a fall in housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20d returns in more than 55% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent drop in real retail sales (RSAFS), signals a contraction in economic output and demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and RSAFS both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six months signals a low-rate, high-inflation regime, compressing real yields and boosting equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60d returns in more than 60% of such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5%) over six months signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumer spending and supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20d returns in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month, especially if accompanied by a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals deteriorating labor market conditions and impending recession, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE jumps > 0.4pp in one month AND PAYEMS falls
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60d returns in more than 50% of such triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity and broader economic expansion, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20d returns in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA for five consecutive months.
